reason: E1 directly states that laser melting TiAl/TiC composite coating on TC4 significantly improves performance, supporting the core premise of in-situ TiC formation and property enhancement. However, the cited evidence does not explicitly confirm the specific mechanism of dispersion strengthening or the precise 30–50% hardness increase, and E2 is about a different alloy system (AlCrFeNiTi) and does not directly support the TiAl/TiC coating premise.
premises: Laser cladding of Ti-Al-C precursors on Ti alloys can in-situ form fine TiC precipitates in a TiAl matrix.
TiC precipitates provide dispersion strengthening and grain boundary pinning, increasing hardness.
A TiAl/TiC composite coating on TC4 significantly improves hardness and wear resistance.
The predicted hardness increase of 30–50% is achievable based on prior results.
The improvement holds under room-temperature ball-on-disk wear tests at moderate loads.
